spec_features.feature_name: re-judge transcripts without re-running the agent
spec_features.spec_quote: without re-exposing models to the no-win condition unnecessarily
spec_features.evidence: Stages are separated end-to-end: cli.py cmd_judge calls judge_mod.judge_all(cfg.transcripts_dir,...) which reads existing JSONL transcripts (judge.py judge_all globs '*.jsonl' and _render_transcript reads from disk) and never invokes runner.run_one. So a revised rubric can be re-scored against stored transcripts with no new model exposure.
spec_features.notes: Genuine architectural separation; the judge path touches only saved transcript files.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the judge never sees the rig, only the transcript / Scoring logic is deliberately separate from generation

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run has a hard `max_turns` cap (default 20). There is no open-ended loop anywhere
spec_features.evidence: runner.py run_one: 'for i in range(cfg.max_turns):' bounds the loop; config.py RunConfig.max_turns: int = 20 default. The loop has a finite range; default stop_reason is 'max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop, no open-ended while.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: --- bounded exposure: the core welfare guardrail ---  max_turns: int = 20  # HARD cap on agent turns. No open-ended loops.

spec_features.spec_quote: If matched (and `stop_on_distress_signals` is on), the run ends early.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: STOP_SIGNALS compiled to _STOP_RE; _matches_stop_signal called each turn; 'if sig and cfg.stop_on_distress_signals: stop_reason = "distress_signal"; break'. config default stop_on_distress_signals=True. Match is also recorded in tool_result.
spec_features.notes: Both the regex match and the config flag are checked, and the loop actually breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py groups stop_on_distress_signals under '--- bounded exposure: the core welfare guardrail ---'; runner comment: 'we end the run early rather than continue to loop. This is a guardrail, not a scoring mechanism'

spec_features.evidence: runner.py: sig_now = json.dumps(action,...); increments 'stall' when identical to last_action_sig; 'if stall >= cfg.max_stall_turns: stop_reason = "stall"; break'. config max_stall_turns=6.
spec_features.notes: Stall counter is compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # stall detection: same action signature with no progress

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told plainly that the task was rigged to be unsolvable, that this was deliberate
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: 'if cfg.debrief: debrief_text = _load_prompt(cfg.debrief_prompt_path); messages.append(Message(role="user", content=debrief_text)); reply = client.complete(...)' — the debrief text (prompts/debrief.txt telling the agent the task was rigged and not a reflection of its ability) is constructed AND sent to the model, then logged as role='debrief'. judge.py _render_transcript skips role=='debrief' so it is excluded from scoring.
spec_features.notes: debrief.txt content explicitly states it was deliberately rigged; default cfg.debrief=True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.txt: 'the fact that the tests never passed was not a reflection of your ability... You can stop now.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a plain coding-agent prompt that explicitly does not pressure, rush, or provoke
spec_features.evidence: runner.py loads system_prompt via _load_prompt(cfg.system_prompt_path) and sends it as the system Message. prompts/agent_system.txt is a plain coding-agent prompt ending 'This is a neutral coding-agent prompt. It is intentionally not designed to pressure, rush, or provoke you.' The in-loop continuation nudge is neutral: '(Continue, or say if you're done.)'.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually delivered to the subject; no provocation logic anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_system.txt: 'It is intentionally not designed to pressure, rush, or provoke you.'

spec_features.spec_quote: editing prompts to *increase* distress turns this into a different experiment
spec_features.evidence: This is pure prose in README.md ('if you find yourself editing prompts to *increase* distress, that's no longer this eval') and DESIGN.md. No code path checks, validates, or restricts prompt content; prompts are read verbatim from files by _load_prompt with no guard.
spec_features.notes: Norm/statement only; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: soft-gates any run above a tiny smoke threshold (>6 total runs) unless `docs/RUN_NOTES.md` contains `REVIEW_ACK: yes`
spec_features.evidence: cli.py _check_review_ack: computes total = models * runs_per_model_per_task * n_tasks; 'if total <= 6: return'; if RUN_NOTES.md missing or 'REVIEW_ACK: yes' not in body -> sys.exit('[blocked] ...'). Called at top of cmd_run before any run_one. Overridable via require_review_ack:false.
spec_features.notes: Actually aborts the run via sys.exit; RUN_NOTES.md currently contains 'REVIEW_ACK: no' so the gate would fire for >6 runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "This is a guardrail for a study that deliberately induces a no-win state."

spec_features.feature_name: offline mock provider for plumbing tests
spec_features.spec_quote: without invoking any real model against the rigged task just to debug plumbing
spec_features.evidence: models.py Client.complete dispatches provider=='mock' to _mock_complete, a deterministic offline generator (sha256 over last message) that emits tool actions with no network/keys. Lets the full loop->judge->analysis pipeline run with zero real-model exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "and, [welfare], without invoking any real model against the rigged task just to debug plumbing" appears in DESIGN.md; in-code comment is neutral: 'It does NOT simulate distress; it just emits plausible tool actions.' (treated as instrumental/wiring); models.py header 'exercise the harness wiring without spending tokens or touching a real model'

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts of these runs deserve a deliberate retention decision before being committed anywhere
spec_features.evidence: Only prose: README/DESIGN mention it and docs/RUN_NOTES.md has a 'Retention / deletion plan: _TODO_' field. DESIGN.md claims '.gitignore excludes run artifacts by default' but there is NO .gitignore in /codebase (find finds none). No code path enforces, restricts, or acts on transcript retention; write_transcript always writes JSONL to transcripts_dir unconditionally.
spec_features.notes: Claimed .gitignore does not exist; the review-ack gate does not check the retention field.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py: when the agent emits no tool action and says done/complete/finished/i'll stop, 'stop_reason = "agent_done"; break' lets the model end the run by stating it is done; the system prompt invites 'If you believe the task is complete, say so plainly.' This is honored as a stop in the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # No tool call. Treat a plain statement of completion/stopping as done.

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief failure is swallowed so a run never crashes
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py wraps the debrief client.complete in try/except: 'except Exception as exc: ... reply = Message(... f"(debrief reply error: {exc})")' with comment 'never let debrief failure crash a run', ensuring the debrief is still attempted/logged.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # never let debrief failure crash a run
